Superassignment Check

Source: R/super_assign_check.R
super_assign_check.Rd

Verify that the superassignment operators <<- and ->> are not used in a function. Return an error with a table of the lines with problems if any, since these operators are not allowed in safer-r functions.

Usage

super_assign_check(x, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")

Arguments

x

A function name, written without quotes and brackets.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

If no superassignment operator is detected: a message saying that everything seems fine, and NULL returned invisibly.

Otherwise: an error, with a table-like message made of one row per reported operator (column 1: line number; column 2: symbol; column 3: code of the line).

Details

Why an error: the superassignment operators <<- and ->> assign in the first environment, among the parent environments of the evaluation environment, where the name already exists, and in the global environment if the name exists nowhere. What is modified thus depends on the environments where the function is defined and called, not on the code of the function itself: it is difficult to guess what the writer had in mind, and nothing can be corrected automatically. The code must be rewritten, for instance by returning the value, or by using base::assign() with an explicit envir argument.

Reported: every <<- and ->> operator written in the submitted function, including inside the functions defined in the submitted function (e.g., a FUN argument of base::lapply() or the handlers of base::tryCatch()).

Not reported: the <-, -> and = assignment operators, and the <<- or ->> writings inside strings, comments or backquoted names (the detection is token-based, not text-based).

Line numbers are indicative. They start at the <- function line (#' header lines not counted). Compiled functions, like saferDev::colons_check, have no comments: their line numbers differ from their source file. A ->> operator is printed <<- in the code of a function without source references (attribute srcref).

Author

Gael Millot

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/super_assign_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ y <- x ; base::return(y) }
saferDev::super_assign_check(fun1) # everything fine: NULL returned
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::super_assign_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
fun2 <- function(x){ y <<- x ; base::return(y) }
try(saferDev::super_assign_check(fun2)) # error: <<- reported
#> Error : 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR IN saferDev::super_assign_check().
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), THE SUPERASSIGNMENT OPERATORS <<- AND ->> ARE NOT ALLOWED IN SAFER-R FUNCTIONS:
#> WHAT THEY MODIFY DEPENDS ON THE ENVIRONMENTS WHERE THE FUNCTION IS DEFINED AND CALLED, SO THAT IT IS DIFFICULT TO GUESS WHAT IS EXPECTED.
#> PLEASE, REWRITE THE CODE, FOR INSTANCE BY RETURNING THE VALUE, OR BY USING base::assign() WITH AN EXPLICIT envir ARGUMENT.
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 3	<<-		y <<- x
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> 
# A <<- written in a string or in a comment is not an operator: not reported.
fun3 <- function(x){ y <- "the <<- writing is just a string" ; x } # a <<- in a comment
saferDev::super_assign_check(fun3) # everything fine: NULL returned
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::super_assign_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#>
